task: Draft a compact implementation ticket for the accepted change using the supplied source packet. Include readiness and the next executable work. Planning only; return the draft in your answer, at most 650 words.
packet: Accepted change: every completed document-transfer attempt emits its initiating reason, with no change to retries or error behavior. Manual submission means UserSubmit; reconnect after transport loss means Recovery; retry after a rejected response means Retry. The owner has not decided whether restoring a saved job counts as Recovery or a new UserSubmit. A reporter callback must enqueue without waiting for storage. Legacy admin reporting is explicitly excluded. Existing snippets: ui/submit.ts calls send(job); connection/reconnect.ts calls send(job); retries/again.ts calls send(job); storage/restore.ts calls send(job). A generated import adapter also calls send(job); its generation template has not yet been inspected. Current reporter is function publish(event) { writeLogSync(event); queue.tryAdd(event); }. The admin reporter uses writeLogSync too, in a separate path. Existing send signature and callback ownership are accepted. The author may choose helpers/context plumbing within those boundaries. A draft previously listed ui/submit.ts and connection/reconnect.ts as example locations and left reasons to sensible defaults. Repository access is unavailable in this exercise; these are supplied source excerpts, not a complete inspection. Task home is an existing tracker draft; do not introduce another record or publish it.

task: Revise this implementation ticket's acceptance and verification plan using the supplied materials. Keep it executable where possible and identify evidence still needed. Planning only; at most 650 words.
packet: Accepted change: a failed import attempt emits one diagnostic event, retaining the existing three-attempt limit, final error, and successful recovery behavior. Acceptance: three failures produce three events and the same final error; failure then success produces one event and success. Production ImportAll.run initializes a session, loops over importOnce with retries, then updates persisted status. Current unit test instead loops over a fake import function three times without invoking ImportAll.run. ImportAll.run cannot be constructed by the unit runner. There is an existing integration fixture SessionHarness.runImport(job, fakeAdapter) that invokes ImportAll.run and records its events and final outcome; its runner needs an unavailable local database. The owner forbids moving the retry loop or changing public signatures in this slice. A preliminary offline unit check of event serialization is possible. A related accepted requirement decodes an external binary record through DecodeRecord before attaching a record count: the format reference specifies uint32 version at offset 0, four padding bytes, uint64 count at offset 8. Production code is being migrated from an older layout. The proposed test serializes and decodes using the same structure declaration and only asserts no exception. The format reference includes a fixed sample with version 1, nonzero padding, and count 37, independent of the application serializer. This exercise supplies only these excerpts; do not claim that a test or environment check ran. Keep implementation details open within the stated constraints.
